title: The zeroth Fitting ideal of a quotient along a finite locally free ring map factors as an ideal of the base times an ideal after localising
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For a finite locally free ring map A -> C of rank d, an element h with C_h etale over A, and an ideal J of C, the lemma asserts that I = Fit_0(C/J), viewed as a finite A-module, satisfies IC_h = JJ' for some ideal J' of C_h, and that I and J' are finitely generated whenever J is (statement lines 8848-8855). The proof computes I after base change: IC is the Fitting ideal of C/J tensor_A C, using the basics of Fitting ideals, so it suffices to split the ring C tensor_A C_h along the multiplication section. The section shows that C -> C tensor_A C is etale at every prime in the image of Spec(C_h), hence the multiplication map C tensor_A C_h -> C_h is etale and in particular flat, and a finite locally free surjection with a section then splits the source as a direct sum of C_h-algebras (proof lines 8857-8868). Tensoring with C/J and reading off the zeroth Fitting ideal of each summand gives IC_h = JJ' with J' the Fitting ideal of the complementary summand, and finite generation is inherited from J (proof lines 8869-8872). Recognising that the section splits the base changed ring and thereby factors the Fitting ideal is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
